text.p: German Finance Minister Theo Waigel said on Wednesday that any early sale of the government's remaining stake in Deutsche Telekom AG would be carried out in such a way that it would not upset the market.
Waigel said the company's landmark listing last November was a success and that its competitive position was strong.
"So I think it would be right that we continue the privatisation in appropriate tranches that are bearable by the stock market," he told reporters in Bonn.
The German government holds 75 percent of Deutsche Telekom shares.
A Deutsche Telekom spokesman said that the sale of the government's stake would only be allowed under the current law if it met the conditions outlined by Telekom chairman Ron Sommer.

Sommer told the daily Bild newspaper in a report to appear on Thursday that German law requires the government to seek approval from the Telekom managment board for a sale of shares that would impact the market before December 31, 1999.

"Such a measure requires the approval of the management board," said Sommer. "We will ensure that the interests of the nearly two million shareholders are not affected. There is complete agreement on this point between the finance minister and myself," he said.
